cells.tense: You are holding a shape for something that is still growing, right now.
cells.ask: Write down the three things that matter most this week, then circle the one you will do first. Tell one person what you chose and why.
cells.core:
You are keeping a shape around something that is still growing, and you are not forcing the growth to hurry. That is harder than it sounds. You make a plan and then leave room inside it. When what comes first is clear to you, the people near you can move too, and some of that likely goes unmentioned.

The thing to watch is not whether the shape is neat. It is whether it is still serving what is inside it. A plan held tighter than the thing it was built for stops being useful. Checking that is the work. Small and steady is how this goes.
cells.sheetLine: You hold a shape that lets the thing grow.
cells.verb: turning what is tangled into a shape someone can move through
cells.place: where something is still growing and needs tending, not forcing

cells.tense: You are building a shape for something that has not happened yet, and holding it hard.
cells.ask: Pick one plan you are protecting and say out loud what it is actually for. If you cannot say it in one sentence, loosen it.
cells.core:
You are building the shape ahead of the thing that will fill it. Somewhere in the future there is a version where this all works, and you are living there, tightening the plan so nothing can slip. The structure was supposed to hold the growing thing. Now the structure is the thing, and it is getting your attention instead.

What that costs you is the growing thing. It cannot tell you what it needs while you are already deciding. Loosening this is not giving up. Something that can be said in one sentence is probably still worth keeping. The rest might just be the plan protecting itself.

cells.tense: The shape went out of things a while back, and you are still standing where it stopped.
cells.ask: Choose the smallest next step you can actually finish today, do it, then stop on purpose and notice what held. Do this again tomorrow.
cells.core:
There was a point where the pieces were going to come together and they did not, and you have been standing there since. Now nothing has a clear place. Priorities do not line up. The days arrive and the sequence is not there. You can see what is around you and you cannot see what comes first.

What has been missing is not effort. It is a shape small enough to hold. Not a system, not a whole rebuild. One thing that finishes, done today, so your hands remember what holding something steady feels like. The care for what is growing is still in you. It just needs something real to point at again.

cells.tense: You are already the one keeping things in order, and you would not say so.
cells.ask: Name one thing you keep in order, out loud, as yours. Ask the person who leans on it what they would do without it.
cells.core:
People around you are steady because of something you do without naming it. The shape is already there. Whatever is being built can be built because you keep the parts in reach, and you would describe yourself as someone who has not figured it out yet. Others would not.

The care and the ordering are the same thing. That is the part that gets missed. When you say you feel formless, that may be true of how you feel and not true of what you do. Naming one thing you keep, without making it small, is how the two versions get close enough to meet. Then the shape you hold can get your full attention instead of your doubt.
